sections.skill: Write a clear request with task, context, audience and limits

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: Which request is clearest?

choices.text: "Write something good about our soap for people, please, thanks."
"Write a 50-word description of our 12-dollar lavender soap for busy parents."

questions.correct_answer: "Write a 50-word description of our 12-dollar lavender soap for busy parents."
questions.intro: An AI tool works better with a clear request (often called a PROMPT). Include: the TASK ("write a 50-word product description"), the CONTEXT (what the product is, price, who makes it), the AUDIENCE ("busy parents"), and any LIMITS (tone, length, words to avoid, facts that must be included). Vague requests like "write something good" give vague results. If the first answer is off, refine the request with specific feedback.

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: "A sandwich" is like what kind of request?
questions.correct_answer: A vague one
questions.intro: If you say "a sandwich," you might get anything. If you say "turkey on wheat, no mayo, toasted, cut in half," you get what you wanted. The order includes what (task), how (limits), and for whom (maybe "for my child, small size"). A clear AI request works the same way. If the sandwich comes out wrong, you tell the person exactly what to fix.
